standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies representability for functors on the abelian category commuting with colimits, which the author upgrades to the derived category setting.

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that idempotents split in the derived category, which turns the representation up to a direct summand into an honest representation.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 2982-2990): the functor on the derived category is assumed to commute with coproducts and to be cohomological, and the author sets up the comparison with the functors it induces on the abelian category.

Representing a direct summand (proof lines 2990-3012): applying the representability result in the abelian setting level by level and comparing the induced maps, the author shows that the functor is a direct summand of a representable functor, the arrow exhibiting the splitting being functorial in the test object.

Splitting idempotents (proof lines 3012-3016): because the derived category is Karoubian, the idempotent producing that summand has an image, which is the object representing the functor, and the proof concludes.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the functor to a collection of functors on the abelian category and represent them.
Compare the resulting representations to exhibit the functor as a direct summand of a representable one.
Use that idempotents split in the derived category to obtain the representing object.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves Brown representability for a cohomological functor on the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category that commutes with coproducts (statement lines 2974-2980). The proof is a complete argument: the functor is compared with the functors it induces on the abelian category and these are represented by the abelian version of the theorem (proof lines 2982-2990); the comparison of the resulting representations exhibits the given functor as a direct summand of a representable functor, with the splitting functorial in the test object (proof lines 2990-3012); and since idempotents split in the derived category, the corresponding image is the representing object (proof lines 3012-3016). The non-formal content is the comparison of the representations and the splitting step. The claim is H2.
